markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (98%)** · Confident · Read in turn

The conformal set, second model and all five similar cases agree on Invasive [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 98%, InSitu 1% | Strongly favors Invasive |
| Conformal set | {Invasive} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 1.00 / percentile 1.0 | No input flag raised |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model concurs |
| Similar cases | 5 of 5 Invasive | Unanimous neighbors |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 3, 7, 11) · ↑ invasive · Scored above typical; concept model links it to invasive [F3] · Validated
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (region 8) · ↑ invasive · Scored below typical; low score associated with invasive · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 6, 7, 11) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; small contribution in the concept model · Validated
- **Frequent mitotic figures** (regions 2, 6, 11) · ↑ invasive · Scored high, but spot check 0/20 [F2] · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions lowers the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60). It is faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion difference is 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007), which includes 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier. This case leans on mitoses and normal lobules (both 0/20, Unreliable).

## Could be wrong if
- The input is a resampled, simulated frozen section (severity 3); the reliability score ranks errors only modestly (AUROC 0.69).
- Region 5 (10%) and region 1 (44%) score low for invasive despite 98% overall.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 3, 7, 11**: confirm tumor infiltrating stroma.
2. **Regions 5, 1**: low regional invasive risk; look for benign or in situ areas.
3. **Regions 2, 6, 11**: look for mitotic figures; the model's mitosis concept failed its spot check.
